items.title: Dutch spelling habits that mislead in pinyin (u/oe/uu, j, g, h, w, z, ui, ie, ou)
items.rule: Read pinyin letters with pinyin values, not Dutch ones: u = Dutch oe [u] (不 bù, 路 lù), except after j/q/x/y and ü, where it is Dutch uu [y] (女 nǚ ≈ Dutch 'nu'); j = [tɕ] (鸡 jī), never Dutch j [j]; g = [k] without a puff (哥 gē), never the Dutch fricative g; h = [x], i.e. the Dutch ch of lachen/acht (好 hǎo), not Dutch h; w = an English-type [w] (我 wǒ), not the Dutch labiodental w; z = [ts] (字 zì), not Dutch z; ui = [u̯eɪ̯] (对 duì), not Dutch ui; ie = [i̯ɛ] (谢 xiè), not Dutch ie [i]; ou = [oʊ̯] (有 yǒu), not Dutch ou [ɑu̯].
items.details: Side-by-side IPA from Wiktionary via WikiPron. Mandarin (cmn): 不 pu, 路 lu, 女 ny, 雞 t͡ɕi, 哥 kɤ, 好 xɑʊ̯, 我 wɔ, 字 t͡sz̩, 對 tu̯eɪ̯, 謝 ɕi̯ɛ, 有 joʊ̯. Dutch (nld): boek buk, doen dun (oe = [u]); vuur vyr, nu ny (uu/u = [y]); ja jaː (j = [j]); goed ɣut (g = [ɣ]); lachen lɑxə, acht ɑxt (ch = [x]); huis ɦœy̯s, hoed ɦut (h = [ɦ]); wat ʋɑt, water ʋaːtər (w = [ʋ]); zee zeː (z = [z]); uit œy̯t (ui = [œy̯]); ziek zik, tien tin (ie = [i]); oud ɑu̯t, jou jɑu̯ (ou = [ɑu̯]). The same IPA symbol in both lists means a close enough sound for a learner; vowel length and fine tongue position still differ.
items.common_mistake: Reading 不 bù with Dutch u or uu, 鸡 jī as 'yee', 哥 gē with a Dutch g, 好 hǎo with a Dutch h, 谢谢 with Dutch ie ('sjiesjie'), 对 duì with Dutch ui, and 有 yǒu with Dutch ou.

items.title: Neutral tone: particles and toneless second syllables (东西 dōngxi vs dōngxī)
items.rule: Some syllables have no tone of their own: they are short and light, and their pitch depends on the syllable before (half-low after a 1st tone, mid after a 2nd, higher after a 3rd, lowest after a 4th). Pinyin writes them without a tone mark (包子 bāozi). The neutral tone is obligatory for grammatical particles — 的/地/得 de, 了 le, 吗 ma, 呢 ne, 吧 ba, aspect 着 zhe and 过 guo — for suffixes such as -们 and -子, for reduplicated kinship terms and verbs (妈妈, 奶奶, 试试), and for the second syllable of many everyday words (谢谢 xièxie, 朋友 péngyou, 喜欢 xǐhuan, 先生 xiānsheng, 衣服 yīfu, 时候 shíhou, 名字 míngzi, 认识 rènshi, 休息 xiūxi, 客气 kèqi). It can distinguish words: 东西 dōngxi 'thing, stuff' vs 东西 dōngxī 'east and west'.
items.details: Official notation (2021 Grading Standards): '必读轻声的音节不标声调，如"包子"标音为"bāozi"'. The 2025 HSK word list prints 东西 dōngxi, 谢谢 xièxie, 朋友 péngyou, 喜欢 xǐhuan, 先生 xiānsheng, 衣服 yīfu, 时候 shíhou, 名字 míngzi, 认识 rènshi, 休息 xiūxi and the particles 了 le, 的 de, 得 de, 地 de, 吗 ma, 呢 ne, 吧 ba. CC-CEDICT: 东西 [dong1 xi1] 'east and west' vs [dong1 xi5] 'thing; stuff; person'. PaddleSpeech's TTS front end makes sentence-final 吧/呢/啊…, word-final 的/地/得, aspect 了/着/过, the suffixes 们/子 and reduplicated nouns/verbs (奶奶, 试试) neutral, and lists 东西, 朋友, 喜欢, 先生, 衣服, 时候, 名字, 认识, 休息, 客气 among its 'must neutral tone' words. Pitch of the neutral syllable (Wiktionary IPA via WikiPron): 包子 …⁵⁵ + ², 朋友 …³⁵ + ³, 你們 …²¹⁴ + ⁴, 謝謝 …⁵¹ + ¹.
items.common_mistake: Giving particles and second syllables a full tone (xièxiè, péngyǒu, a rising má for 吗), which makes speech choppy, and reading 东西 'thing' as dōngxī.

examples.english: thing, stuff (neutral xi)

items.title: 了 is not a past-tense marker
items.rule: 了 marks aspect, not tense. Verb + 了 (了1) presents an action as completed, typically with a counted object: 他买了一本书. Sentence-final 了 (了2) signals a change of state or a new situation: 我累了, 下雨了, 她病了 — and works for the future too: 要下雨了 'it's going to rain', 我们快要放假了. A past event is negated with 没(有) + verb and no 了: 他没买书, 他没吃早饭 (not *他没买了书). Past states, and past events whose time or manner is in focus with 是…的 or 才, usually take no 了 (当时我很讨厌爸爸; 我是昨天到北京的; 我今天八点才起床).
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 21】动态助词：了1 — 他买了一本书。／他没买书。我写了两个汉字。／我没写汉字。; 【一 40】变化态 (了2) — 她病了。／她没病。雨小了。／雨没小。他吃早饭了。／他没吃早饭。; 【一 41】完成态 — 他买了两个面包。／他没买面包。; 【一 31】下雨了。; 【二 81】要／快要／就要……了 — 要下雨了。我们快要放假了。; 【二 60】是……的 — 我是昨天到北京的。; 【二 20】才 — 我今天八点才起床。 CC-CEDICT 了 [le5]: '(completed action marker); (modal particle indicating change of state, situation now)'. Learner corpora: YACLC '当时，我不明白我父亲的想法，很讨厌爸爸了。' corrected to '…很讨厌爸爸。'; MuCGEC '…我没学了新的东西。' corrected to '…我没学到新的东西' / '…我没学新的东西'.
items.common_mistake: Treating 了 as English '-ed': adding it to past states (*当时我很讨厌爸爸了 — attested in YACLC) and keeping it after 没 (*我没学了新的东西 — attested in MuCGEC).

examples.english: He bought a book. (completed action: verb + 了 + counted object)

items.title: 不 vs 没(有): 'not' vs 'didn't / doesn't have'
items.rule: 不 negates what is or will be the case — states, adjectives, habits, intentions and future actions: 今天不热, 他不去医院 'he isn't going to the hospital'. 没 or 没有 negates that something happened (past or completed actions), without 了: 他昨天没上课, 我今天没有吃早饭. 有 'to have / there is' is only ever negated with 没: 他没有哥哥, 房间里没有桌子 (never *不有).
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 14】否定副词：别、不、没、没有 — 今天不热。他昨天没上课。我今天没有吃早饭。; 【一 29】他不去医院。; 【一 37】"有"字句 — 我有很多书。他没有哥哥。房间里没有桌子。; 【一 40】他吃早饭了。／他没吃早饭。 CC-CEDICT: 没 [mei2] '(negative prefix for verbs) have not; not'; 没有 [mei2 you3] 'haven't; hasn't; doesn't exist; to not have; to not be'; 不 [bu4] 'no; not so; (bound form) not; un-'. A related learner error (MuCGEC): '吸烟虽然对健康不有利' corrected to '…对健康不利'.
items.common_mistake: *不有 for 'don't have', and 不 for an event that did not happen (it needs 没: 他昨天没上课).

examples.english: It isn't hot today. (state: 不)

items.title: Number + measure word + noun (一个人, 两本书)
items.rule: A number cannot attach directly to a noun: a measure word (classifier) goes in between — 两本书 'two books', 一件衣服 'a piece of clothing', 三口人 'three people (in a family)'; after 这, 那, 哪, 几 and 每 a measure word is normally used as well (那个书包 'that schoolbag', 这个房间 'this room'). 个 is the general measure word for people and for nouns without a special one, and is usually toneless after a number (一个 yí ge, 两个 liǎng ge). Common specific ones: 本 books; 张 flat things such as paper and tables; 杯 a cup/glass of; 位 people (polite); 只 many animals and one of a pair; 件 clothes and matters; 条 long thin things (rivers, roads, trousers) and dogs; 辆 vehicles. 个 can stand in for some specific measure words, so it is the safe default, but 本/杯/位/张 are expected with their nouns.
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 08】名量词：杯、本、个、家、间、口、块、页 — 两杯牛奶 三本书 四个学生 五家商店 六间房子 三口人 七块面包; 【二 10】名量词：层、封、件、条、位 — 两层楼 一封信 一件衣服 一条河 一位老师; 【一 23】数量短语 — 一个 两杯 三本 四包 五块; 【一 06】— 她喜欢那个书包。 2025 HSK grammar syllabus: HSK1 专用名量词 本、个、家、口、块、件、只、元 and 借用名量词 杯; HSK2 条、位、间、名; HSK3 把、双、张、种、层、封、页、辆…. CC-CEDICT: 个 '(classifier used before a noun that has no specific classifier)'; 本 'classifier for books, periodicals, files etc'; 张 'classifier for flat objects, sheet'; 杯 'classifier for certain containers of liquids: glass, cup'; 位 'classifier for people (honorific)'; 只 'classifier for birds and certain animals, one of a pair, some utensils…'; 件 'classifier for events, things, clothes etc'; 条 'classifier for long thin things (ribbon, river, road, trousers etc)'; 辆 'classifier for vehicles'; noun entries: 书 CL:本, 车 CL:辆, 纸 CL:张, 桌子 CL:张, 衣服 CL:件, 狗 CL:只/条, 裤子 CL:条, 老师 CL:个/位, 咖啡 CL:杯. 新华字典 个: '用于没有专用量词的事物…也可用于某些有专用量词的事物'. Toneless 个 after numerals: CC-CEDICT 一个 [yi1 ge5]; PaddleSpeech '个做量词' → neutral.
items.common_mistake: Leaving the measure word out, as in English 'one student' (*只有一学生 — attested in YACLC, corrected to 一个学生 / 一名学生).

examples.english: two books (本 for books)

items.title: 的, 地, 得: three particles, one sound (de)
items.rule: As particles all three are pronounced de with a neutral tone, so the difference shows in writing (chat messages, email): 的 comes before a noun (modifier + 的 + noun: 你的衣服, 干净的房间); 地 comes before a verb (adverbial + 地 + verb: 高兴地说 'said happily'); 得 comes after a verb or adjective and introduces a complement of degree or possibility (跑得很快 'runs fast', 听得懂 'can understand'). Quick test: …的 + noun, …地 + verb, verb + 得 + …
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 20】结构助词：的1、地 — 你的衣服很好看。他高兴地说："我明天回家。"; 【一 27】我喜欢干净的房间。; 【二 31】结构助词：得 — 他走得有点儿快。她篮球打得很不错。; 【二 51】状态补语 — 她跑得很快。我们玩儿得很高兴。; 【三 48】可能补语 — 老师的话我都听得懂。 2025 HSK word list: 的 de 助 (HSK1); 得 de 助 and 地 de 助 (HSK2), while 得 dé 'to get' and 地 dì 'ground' (HSK3) keep full tones. CC-CEDICT: 的 [de5] '(used after an attribute when it modifies a noun)'; 地 [de5] '-ly; structural particle: used before a verb or adjective, linking it to preceding modifying adverbial adjunct'; 得 [de5] 'structural particle: used after a verb (or adjective as main verb), linking it to following phrase indicating effect, degree, possibility etc'. Learner errors: MuCGEC '有的孩子从小就开始拼命的学习。' → '…拼命地学习。'; YACLC '这个星期的时间过的很愉快' → '…过得很愉快'; YACLC '跟他们的相处的更愉快' → '跟他们相处得更愉快'. Automatic pinyin can get this wrong too: the pinyin-pro library used as a second opinion by check.mjs reads 高兴地 as dì and 跑得很快 as dé.
items.common_mistake: Writing 的 for all three (*过的很愉快, *拼命的学习 — both attested in learner corpora), and reading 得/地 with their other dictionary readings (dé 'to get', dì 'ground') when they are particles.

examples.english: Your clothes look nice. (的 + noun)

items.title: 二 èr vs 两 liǎng
items.rule: Both mean 'two'. Use 两 before a measure word (两个人, 两本书, 两杯) and for clock time (两点 2:00 — but 两点二十五 2:25 and 十二点 12:00); before 千, 万 and 亿 两 is usual (两千, 两万), though 二 also occurs. Use 二 when counting or reading out numbers (一、二、三; phone, room and bus numbers are read digit by digit with 二, never 两, and 1 is then often said yāo 幺 for clarity), for the tens and units of a larger number (十二, 二十, 一千三百五十二, 二十位学生), in ordinals (第二, 二楼 'second floor', 二月 'February') and in decimals and fractions (零点二四, 五分之二). For 200 both 二百 and 两百 are used; inside a longer number the 现代汉语词典 gives 二 for the hundreds (二百二十二). With traditional weights both work (两斤 or 二斤), but two of the unit 两 is always 二两. A few polite set phrases keep 二 before 位: 二位, 您二位 'you two (polite)'.
items.details: 新华字典, entry 两: '一般用在量词或"半、千、万、亿"等前面…在多位数中常是大数用"两"，小数用"二"（"两"和"二"也可通用）'; '⑴有的数目字只能用"二"不能用"两"，如一、二、三，二十等中的"二"；⑵小数和分数只能用"二"…如零点二四（0.24），五分之二等；⑶序数也只能用"二"…如二姐，第二名等'; '③在传统的度量衡单位前，"两"和"二"可通用 两斤（二斤）。但"二两"不能用成"两两"。④新的度量衡单位前，一般用"两" 两米、两吨'. 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 07】数词 — 十二 二十 二百 两百 / 两个人 两本书; 【一 44】钟点 — 两点 (2:00), 两点二十五（分）, 差两分八点; 【二 09】— 一千三百五十二, 两万一千四百六十五; 【二 72】序数 — 第一 第三 第七 二楼 三层; other examples: 我们班由两位老师和二十位学生组成。都十二点了。机票差不多要两千块钱。卡里只有二百块钱。 Wiktionary (WikiPron) has 二月 ˀɤɻ⁵¹⁻⁵³ ɥɛ⁵¹ and 第二. CC-CEDICT 幺 [yao1]: 'one (unambiguous spoken form when spelling out numbers, esp. on telephone or in military)'. Learner errors (MuCGEC): '我不喜欢流行歌曲是有二个原因。' → '…有两个原因。'; '我去过了北京二次' → '我去过北京两次'. Reviewer (2026-11-02): 现代汉语词典 (7th ed.), entry 两: '读数目字只用"二"不用"两"…小数和分数只用"二"…序数也只用"二"…在一般量词前，用"两"不用"二"。在传统的度量衡单位前，"两"和"二"一般都可用，用"二"为多（"二两"不能说"两两"）。新的度量衡单位前一般用"两"…在多位数中，百、十、个位用"二"不用"两"，如"二百二十二"。"千、万、亿"的前面，"两"和"二"一般都可用'; entry 您: '～二位想吃点儿什么？'. Official HSK 1 sample H10901: '你住在哪儿？' — '我和妈妈都住在一零二。' (a room number read digit by digit).
items.common_mistake: Using 二 before a measure word (*二个原因, *去过北京二次 — both attested in MuCGEC); the reverse (两 in 十二, 二十, 第二 or 二月) is wrong by the dictionary rules.

items.title: 会, 能, 可以: three words for 'can'
items.rule: 会 = know how to (a learned skill: 我不会说中文, 他一句中文也不会说) and also 'will, be likely to' in predictions (他病了，今天大概不会来上课了; 我今年也许会去中国学习中文). 能 = be able to / be in a position to, when ability or circumstances decide (明天你能来吗? 'can you make it tomorrow?'); 不能 often means 'must not / you can't' (筷子不能那样拿). 可以 = may, be allowed to (老师，我可以进来吗? 这儿不可以停车). Requests and permission overlap: both 能 and 可以 are used (我能用用你的手机吗? 你能再给我发一下儿吗?). For a learned skill the default is 会.
items.details: CC-CEDICT: 会 [hui4] 'can; to have the skill; to know how to; to be likely to; to be sure to'; 能 [neng2] 'can; to be able to; might possibly'; 可以 [ke3 yi3] 'can; may; possible; able to'. 新华字典 会 ⒋ '能，可能，善于 共产主义一定会实现。他会开飞机。' 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 02】能愿动词：会、能 — 我不会说中文。明天你能来吗？; 【二 01】能愿动词 (1) 可能 (2) 可以 — 老师，我可以进来吗？这儿不可以停车。; 【二 04】我能用用你的手机吗？; 【二 07】筷子不能那样拿。; 【二 19】我今年也许会去中国学习中文。; level 3: 他病了，今天大概不会来上课了。他一句中文也不会说。你的文件我打不开，你能再给我发一下儿吗？ The 2025 HSK grammar syllabus lists 会、能、想、要、可以 as HSK1 modal verbs. Learner error (YACLC): '我希望早就修理，要不然我不会洗澡啊。' corrected to '…要不然我不能洗澡啊。' — the problem was a broken shower (circumstance), not a missing skill. (Example sentence 我不会说中文 is not used below because the checker's segmentation reads 说中 as one word.)
items.common_mistake: Using 会 for circumstances (*要不然我不会洗澡 about a broken shower — attested in YACLC; it should be 不能) and translating every English 'can' with one word.

examples.pinyin: Tā yī jù Zhōngwén yě bù huì shuō.
examples.spoken: Tā yí jù Zhōngwén yě bú huì shuō.
examples.english: He can't speak a word of Chinese. (会 = learned skill)

items.title: 您们 is not the polite plural: use 大家, 各位 or 你们
items.rule: 您 nín is the polite 'you'. It is mostly said to one person. For several people the 新华字典 advises against adding 们 and gives 您俩 or 您二位 (two), 您仨 or 您三位 (three), 您诸位 (more); the 现代汉语词典 glosses 您 as '你；你们（含敬意）' with the example 您二位想吃点儿什么？. In everyday speech a group is addressed as 你们, 大家 'everyone' or 各位 'everybody, ladies and gentlemen' (各位朋友，下午好!). 您们 is not in CC-CEDICT, the 现代汉语词典 or the HSK pronoun lists; some native speakers do write it (rarely), so you may see it, but don't use it yourself.
items.details: 新华字典 您: '注意用于多数时不加词尾"们"，两个人称"您俩"或"您二位"，三个人称"您仨"或"您三位"，三个人以上称"您诸位"。' CC-CEDICT: no entry 您们; 您 'you (courteous, as opposed to informal 你)'; 各位 'everybody; all (guests, colleagues etc); all of you'; 大家 'everyone'. 2025 HSK grammar syllabus HSK1 人称代词: 我、你、您、他、她、我们、你们、他们、她们、它、它们、大家; 各位 is an HSK4 word (and an HSK3 指示代词 in the 2021 Standards: 各位朋友，下午好！). WikiPron lists a Wiktionary entry 您們 (nín + men). A learner wrote '…非常麻烦您们了,谢谢您.' (YACLC); one annotator corrected it to '麻烦你们了,谢谢你们！' while another left 您们 — usage is not uniform, but standard references avoid it. Reviewer (2026-11-02): 现代汉语词典 (7th ed.) 【您】nín '人称代词。你；你们（含敬意）：老师，您早！｜您二位想吃点儿什么？' (no entry 您们). In two corpora of native-speaker task dialogues (CrossWOZ, RiSAWOZ; about 236,000 utterances) 您们 occurs 12 times, always an agent addressing a group (我建议您们可以去狮子林), against 806 for 你们. Official HSK 4 sample H41001: a hotel guest tells the staff '谢谢！麻烦你们了。'.
items.common_mistake: Building a 'polite plural' 您们 by analogy with 你们 when greeting a partner's family or a group of clients; use 大家, 各位 (各位朋友，下午好!) or simply 你们.

items.title: Replying to 谢谢: 不客气, 不用谢, 没事 — 没关系 answers an apology
items.rule: Answer thanks with 不客气 (bú kèqi, literally 'don't be polite'), 不用客气, 别客气 ('no need to stand on ceremony') or 不用谢 ('no need to thank me'); casually also 没事 ('it's nothing'; also said with erhua, 没事儿). In native-speaker dialogues 不客气 is by far the commonest reply, followed by 不用客气 and 别客气. 没关系 'it doesn't matter' is the standard reply to an apology (对不起 → 没关系); after thanks it turns up only occasionally, so keep it for apologies. 没事 fits both. Note that 不客气 also has an ordinary meaning 'impolite, blunt' when it describes how someone behaves.
items.details: CC-CEDICT: 不客气 'you're welcome; don't mention it; impolite; rude; blunt'; 不用谢 'You're welcome. Don't mention it'; 不用客气 'you're welcome; don't mention it; no need to stand on ceremony'; 没事 'it's not important; it's nothing; never mind; to have nothing to do; to be free; to be all right'; 没事儿 '…it's not important; it's nothing; never mind'; 没关系 'it doesn't matter'. 2025 HSK syllabus: 谢谢 xièxie, 不客气 bú kèqi, 没关系 méi guānxi, 没事 méishì and 对不起 duìbuqǐ are all HSK1 words, and the HSK1 task list asks learners to exchange simple courtesies '如你好、谢谢、对不起、再见等'. The 2021 Standards use 没事儿 in '他笑着说："没事儿。"'. Reviewer (2026-11-02): official HSK sample scripts answer thanks with 不客气 (H10901 '谢谢你们！—不客气。再见。'; H21003 '谢谢你！—不客气！再见。'; H41001 '谢谢！麻烦你们了。—不客气。'). 现代汉语词典 不 ❽ '不用；不要（限用于某些客套话）：不谢｜不送｜不客气'. CrossWOZ (5,677 thanks turns) / RiSAWOZ (10,633): replies start with 不客气 55% / 41%, 不用客气 12% / 11%, 别客气 1% / 11%, 不用谢 4% / 4%, 没事 0.7% / 0.3%, 没关系 0.1% / 1.4% (together about 16,300 replies: 不客气 46%, 不用客气 11%, 别客气 8%, 不用谢 4%, 没关系 0.9%). CC-CEDICT: 别客气 'don't mention it; no formalities, please'. The same corpora write 没事 (without 儿) 287 times and 没事儿 17 times.
items.common_mistake: Mixing up the two textbook pairs (谢谢 → 不客气; 对不起 → 没关系): 没关系 after thanks is heard now and then, but it is not the usual reply. And saying 不客气 with a full bù (it is bú kèqi).

items.title: 对不起 vs 不好意思 vs 抱歉; 打扰一下 / 请问 for 'excuse me'
items.rule: 对不起 is the full apology ('I'm sorry'), for something you did wrong (对不起，我错了; after being told you broke a rule: 对不起，我马上离开). Staff also use it to soften bad news or a refusal (对不起，十四号的已经卖完了 'sorry, the 14th is sold out'). 不好意思 is lighter ('sorry, I feel bad about this'): small lapses, inconveniencing someone, interrupting, asking a favour (不好意思，我没拿来); it is also the usual everyday 'excuse me'. 抱歉 'sorry' sounds a little more formal and is very common in service language and announcements (抱歉，先生，这里禁止吸烟; 很抱歉地通知您). To get attention or start a question, use 请问 ('may I ask…'), 打扰一下 ('sorry to bother you') or 不好意思. 劳驾 'excuse me' also exists but is rare in everyday use, and the 2025 HSK syllabus places it in the advanced 7–9 band.
items.details: CC-CEDICT: 对不起 'I'm sorry; excuse me; I beg your pardon; to let (sb) down; to disappoint'; 不好意思 'to feel embarrassed; to find it embarrassing; to be sorry (for inconveniencing sb)'; 抱歉 'to be sorry; to feel apologetic; sorry!'; 打扰 'to disturb; to bother; to trouble'; 请问 'Excuse me, may I ask...?'; 劳驾 'excuse me'. 2025 HSK syllabus levels: 对不起 and 请问 HSK1; 不好意思 HSK2; 抱歉 and 打扰 HSK4; 劳驾 HSK7–9. Official sample listening dialogue: '女：抱歉，先生，这里禁止吸烟。男：对不起，我马上离开。这附近哪里能吸烟？' Official sample reading item: '（打扰）一下，同学，请不要在自习室里大声讨论。' 2021 Standards 【二 50】: '甲：你的词典呢？乙：不好意思，我没拿来。' Reviewer (2026-11-02): official HSK sample scripts — H20901 '对不起，我错了。' and '对不起，十四号的已经卖完了'; H41001 '先生，对不起，我们这儿不能抽烟。'; HSK 4 sample '乘客您好，我们很抱歉地通知您，由于天气原因…'. 现代汉语词典: 对不起 '对人有愧，常用为表示抱歉的套语：～，让您久等了'; 抱歉 '心中不安，觉着对不住别人'; 劳驾 '客套话，用于请别人做事或让路'. CrossWOZ + RiSAWOZ: agents apologise with 抱歉 2,822×, 不好意思 1,106×, 对不起 310×; customers' turns contain 不好意思 106×, 抱歉 17×, 对不起 6× (mostly for their own slips: typos, wrong requests); 请问 3,540×, 打扰一下 6×, 劳驾 5×.
items.common_mistake: Using 对不起 as an all-purpose 'excuse me' — it is the heavier apology; to stop someone or ask a question use 请问, 打扰一下 or 不好意思.

items.title: No 是 before adjectives: 我很忙, not *我是忙
items.rule: Chinese adjectives are predicates by themselves, so there is no 'to be' before them: 我很忙 'I'm busy', 房间很干净 'the room is clean', 今天不冷 'it isn't cold today'. 是 links a subject to a noun (他是我的老师). In a plain positive statement the adjective normally takes a degree adverb — usually 很, which here often does not mean 'very' — or 非常, 太…了, 最, or is negated with 不. 是 + adjective + 的 is a different pattern that classifies (花是白的 'the flowers are white ones'). A stressed 是 before 很 + adjective is not 'to be' either: it means 'indeed, it really is' and is used to agree or concede (你说得对，这位经理是很负责 'you're right, this manager really is responsible'). So 是 never translates a plain 'is / am / are' before an adjective (*我是忙).
items.details: CC-CEDICT: 是 'to be (followed by substantives only)'; 很 'very; quite; (also, often used before an adjective without intensifying its meaning, i.e. as a meaningless syntactic element)'. 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 30】形容词谓语句 — 房间很干净。这个学生最认真。; 【一 25】今天不冷。这个菜很好吃。; 【一 05】她很高。; 【一 36】"是"字句 (1) 他是我的老师。(2) 表示说明或特征 — 花是白的。衣服是干净的。; level 3: 这星期我很忙，要上课，要准备考试，另外，还要参加一些学校活动。 Learner corpora: YACLC '她也是很苗条' → '她很苗条'; MuCGEC '这是很有意思。' → '这很有意思。'; YACLC '去关西大学半路上的马路上拥挤。' → '…马路上很拥挤。' (annotators added 很 to a bare adjective). Reviewer (2026-11-02): emphatic 是 — 2021 Standards 【三 77】用"是"强调: '你说得对，这位经理是很负责。我同意，那电影是很有意思。'; 现代汉语词典 是³ ⑪ '（必须重读）表示坚决肯定，含有"的确、实在"的意思：我打听清楚了，他那天是没去｜这本书是好，你可以看看。'
items.common_mistake: Translating 'is / am / are' as 是 before an adjective (*我是忙, *她也是很苗条 — attested in YACLC; *这是很有意思 — attested in MuCGEC), or leaving a positive adjective bare where annotators add 很 (马路上拥挤 → 马路上很拥挤).

examples.english: The room is clean. (adjective predicate with 很, no 是)

items.title: 比 comparisons take no 很
items.rule: In A 比 B + adjective the adjective stands on its own: 我朋友比我高 'my friend is taller than me'. To say 'even more' use 更 or 还 before the adjective (他的手机比我的更贵; 今天比昨天还凉快); to say by how much, put the amount after the adjective (姐姐比我大两岁; 房间外边比里边凉快一些); for 'much more', put 多了 or 得多 after it (他比我强多了). Do not add 很 (*花钱比赚钱很少).
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 38】比较句1 (1) A比B＋形容词 — 我朋友比我高。这个手机比那个贵。(2) A没有B＋形容词 — 昨天没有今天热。; 【二 58】比较句2 (1) A比B＋形容词＋数量补语 — 姐姐比我大两岁。房间外边比里边凉快一些。(2) A比B＋更／还＋形容词 — 他的手机比我的更贵。今天比昨天还凉快。 None of the official 比 patterns contains 很. Learner corpus (YACLC): '最重要的是花钱比赚钱很少。' → '最重要的是花钱比赚钱少。'; '明天可能复习比今天的复习很好。' → '明天可能复习得比今天更好。' Reviewer (2026-11-02): 现代汉语词典 比 ❾ '用来比较性状和程度的差别：今天的风比昨天更大了｜许多同志都比我强' (no 很); 多¹ ❺ '表示相差的程度大：他比我强多了｜这样摆好看得多'; 2025 syllabus HSK2 比较句1 '（2）A比B+形容词+数量补语/程度补语'.
items.common_mistake: Adding 很 inside a 比 comparison (*花钱比赚钱很少 — attested in YACLC); use 更/还 before the adjective or an amount after it.

examples.english: My friend is taller than me.

items.title: Question words stay in place, and a what/where/who question takes no 吗
items.rule: For a wh-question keep statement order and put the question word in the slot where the answer will go: 你买什么? — 我买一个面包; 你们去哪儿?; 谁是老师?; 你怎么去医院? There is no inversion and no 'do'. 吗 turns a statement into a yes/no question (他是老师吗?); a question that asks 'what / where / who / how' takes no 吗. 吗 and a question word do meet in two common patterns: when the question word means 'any-/some-' the sentence is a yes/no question (有什么推荐吗? 'Any recommendations?'; 还有什么需要帮助的吗? 'Anything else I can help with?'; compare 我好像在哪儿见过你 'I think I've seen you somewhere'), and when the question is tucked inside a yes/no question after a verb such as 知道 'know' or 告诉 'tell' (你知道这个酒店在哪里吗? 'Do you know where the hotel is?').
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 04】疑问代词 — 你们去哪儿？你买什么？谁是老师？你怎么去医院？车站在哪里？; 【一 29】我买一个面包。; 【一 33】(1) 是非问句 他是老师吗？ (2) 特指问句 谁跟你一起去书店？你想买什么？; 【一 45】用"吗"提问 — 他是老师吗？这包子好吃吗？; 【一 46】我们在哪儿见面？你星期天做什么？; 【三 07】不定指用法 — 我好像在哪儿见过你。 CC-CEDICT 吗 [ma5]: '(question particle for "yes-no" questions)'; 什么 'what?; something; anything'. 哪儿 and 哪里 are both standard (both are in the HSK1 question-word list). Reviewer (2026-11-02): 2021 Standards 【三 07】(2) 不定指用法: '我好像在哪儿见过你。你们先吃点儿什么再去公园吧。要是你一个人搬不动，就请谁来帮一下儿吧。'; 现代汉语词典 哪里 ❸ '虚指某一处所：我好像在哪里见过他'. Native task dialogues (CrossWOZ, RiSAWOZ): 3,401 utterances match 什么…吗？ (有什么推荐吗？ 周边还有什么景点吗？ 还有什么需要帮助的吗？) and 126 match 哪儿/哪里…吗？, mostly 你知道这个酒店在哪里吗？.
items.common_mistake: Fronting the question word as in English or Dutch (*哪儿你们去? for 'Where are you going?' / 'Waar ga je heen?') and adding 吗 to a what/where/who question (*你们去哪儿吗? for 'Where are you going?'). 吗 with a question word is fine only when the word means 'any-/some-' (有什么推荐吗?) or when the question is embedded after 知道 / 告诉 (你知道…在哪里吗?).

examples.english: Where are you going? (哪儿 stays after the verb)

items.title: Time and place go before the verb
items.rule: Basic order is Subject – Time – Place – Verb – Object: 我每天在家学习 'I study at home every day' (and in the same way 我明天在家工作 'I'm working from home tomorrow'). Time words (今天, 明天, 每天, 十点, 下午) go before the verb, after the subject or at the very start (他十点睡觉; 明天下雨，我们在家休息). A place phrase with 在 also comes before the verb (哥哥在北京学中文; 她在网上买了两本书). English and Dutch put both after the verb ('I work at home tomorrow', 'Ik werk morgen thuis'). Exception: after a few verbs of position or placement (住 'live', 坐 'sit', 放 'put') 在 + place follows the verb and says where someone is or where something ends up: 你住在哪儿？ 'Where do you live?', 老师把书放在桌子上了, 这些书不能放在外边.
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 28】状语 — 表示时间、处所的词语作状语: 他十点睡觉。我们下午去吧。她在网上买了两本书。; 【一 15】我们从星期一到星期五工作。; 【一 16】在 — 哥哥在北京学中文。他在手机上看电影。; 【二 66】明天下雨，我们在家休息。; 【五 33】多项状语 — 他昨天在教室里认真地写完了作业。她为了通过考试昨天在家复习了一整天。 (time, place, manner, then the verb); 【三 47】example 这些书不能放在外边，应该拿进去。 2025 HSK grammar syllabus HSK1: 状语 '表示时间、处所的词语作状语'. Learner corpus (YACLC): '每天我学习在家，我做作业，写汉字，复习旧课词语。' corrected to '每天我在家学习，…' / '我每天在家学习，…'. 我明天在家工作 is a slot variant (明天, 工作) of the corrected sentence. Reviewer (2026-11-02): official HSK 1 sample H10901 '你住在哪儿？—我和妈妈都住在一零二。'; HSK 3 sample H31003 '他现在住在公司附近。'; 2021 Standards '他却坐在教室里面不动' and 【三 54】'主语＋把＋宾语＋动词＋在／到＋处所：老师把书放在桌子上了。'; 现代汉语词典 哪里 ❶ '你住在哪里？'.
items.common_mistake: Putting the place (or time) after the verb as in English or Dutch (*每天我学习在家 — attested in YACLC).

examples.english: He goes to bed at ten. (time before the verb)

items.title: 和 joins nouns and short phrases, not sentences
items.rule: 和 (and 跟) means 'and' between words or short phrases, mostly nouns and pronouns: 我和弟弟都学习中文, 爸爸跟妈妈都不在家 (also nouns made from verbs: 人们的学习和工作 'people's study and work'). It is not used to join two clauses the way English 'and' is: 我喜欢看电视，弟弟喜欢打球 needs no connector (or use 也, 还, 而且, 然后 as the meaning requires). In lists, separate the items with the enumeration comma 、 and put 和 before the last item without a comma: 北京、台北、香港、澳门和成都.
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 19】连接词或短语：跟2、还是、和2 — 爸爸跟妈妈都不在家。我和弟弟都学习中文。; 【一 39】并列复句 (1) 不用关联词语 — 我喜欢看电视，弟弟喜欢打球。(2) ……，也…… — 我喜欢唱歌，弟弟也喜欢唱歌。 The 2025 HSK grammar syllabus classifies 和2 under '连接词语或短语' and lists clause connectors separately ('连接分句或者句子：但、但是、那、虽然、还是2、因为2、所以'; HSK3 adds 不但、而且、如果、可是、然后). Learner corpora: MuCGEC '我觉得我们每个人都应该进自己的责任，和不浪费能源。' corrected to '…尽自己的责任，不浪费能源。'; YACLC '北京，台北，香港，澳门，和成都' corrected to '北京、台北、香港、澳门和成都'. Reviewer (2026-11-02): the 2025 syllabus lists 和2 under '连接词语或短语' (words or phrases, not only nouns); HSK oral sample: '…会影响人们的学习和工作。'; 现代汉语词典 和² ❸ '〈连〉表示联合；跟；与：工人和农民都是国家的主人'; 顿号 '表示句子内部并列词语之间的停顿'.
items.common_mistake: Using 和 like English 'and' between clauses (*…尽自己的责任，和不浪费能源 — attested in MuCGEC) and the English serial comma before 和 in lists (*澳门，和成都 — attested in YACLC).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé dìdi dōu xuéxí Zhōngwén.
examples.english: My younger brother and I both study Chinese. (和 joins two nouns)

items.title: 也 and 都 go after the subject, right before the verb
items.rule: 也 'also, too' and 都 'all, both' are adverbs: they come after the subject and before the verb (or before 是, 很, 不): 他是学生，我也是学生 'he's a student and so am I'; 同学们都很认真; 爸爸跟妈妈都不在家. 也 never goes in front of the subject the way English 'Also, …' does (*也他比我强 → 他也比我强). 都 'all' sums up the people or things named before it; only in a question can it point ahead to the question word (它家都有什么推荐菜？ 'What dishes do they recommend?'). A 都 at the very start of a sentence is a different use, e.g. 'already': 都十二点了 'it's already twelve o'clock'.
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 13】关联副词：还1、也 — 他是学生，我也是学生。; 【一 10】范围、协同副词：都1 — 同学们都很认真。; 【一 19】爸爸跟妈妈都不在家。我和弟弟都学习中文。; 【一 39】我喜欢唱歌，弟弟也喜欢唱歌。 2025 HSK grammar syllabus HSK1: 范围副词 都1; 关联副词 还1、也. Learner corpus (MuCGEC): '但是他比我高，也他比我强' corrected to '…他也比我强' / '…也比我强'; YACLC '联明天也我们都不知道…' corrected to '连明天我们都不知道…'. Reviewer (2026-11-02): 现代汉语词典 都 ❶ '表示总括，除疑问句外，所总括的成分放在"都"前'; ❹ '表示"已经"：饭都凉了'; 2021 Standards 【二 20】语气副词 都2: '都十二点了，我们该睡觉了。'. CrossWOZ: '它家都有什么推荐菜呀' (14×).
items.common_mistake: Putting 也 (or 都) in front of the subject like English 'Also, …' (*也他比我强 — attested in MuCGEC; *也我们都… — attested in YACLC).

facts.title: Travelling in mainland China with a Dutch passport

facts.question: Can a Dutch (Netherlands) ordinary-passport holder enter mainland China without a visa today? Since when, for how many days and for which purposes?
facts.answer: Yes. Under China's unilateral visa-exemption policy, Dutch citizens with a valid ordinary passport may enter mainland China without a visa for business, tourism, family visits (visiting relatives and friends), exchange visits and transit, and stay up to 30 days per entry. The Netherlands has been covered since 00:00 on 1 December 2023 (Beijing time). The first trial allowed 15 days (business, tourism, family visits, transit) and was extended in May 2024 to 31 December 2025, still with 15 days. From 30 November 2024 the stay became 30 days and 'exchange visits' became an allowed purpose. The Chinese Embassy in the Netherlands' notice of 4 November 2025 extends the policy until 24:00 on 31 December 2026 (Beijing time). Visiting a partner's family falls under 'family visit'. Work, study and news reporting are not covered and still need a visa.

facts.question: What is the 240-hour visa-free transit policy (conditions, ports), and does it apply to Dutch passport holders?
facts.answer: Yes, the Netherlands is on the list. Since 20 August 2026 the policy covers 57 countries; Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam were added then, and the count was 55 after Indonesia joined in June 2025. 40 of the 57 are European, including the Netherlands. Conditions from the National Immigration Administration (NIA): an ordinary passport valid for at least 3 months; an onward interline ticket with a confirmed date and seat to a third country or region, leaving within 240 hours (10 days); entry through one of 65 designated ports in 24 provincial-level regions, then staying within the permitted areas; completing the arrival card and cooperating with checks. There were 60 ports until 5 November 2025, when five Guangdong ports were added. The 240 hours run from 00:00 on the day after entry. Short-term tourism, business, visits and family visits are allowed; work, study and journalism still need a visa. Separately, any nationality may make a 24-hour direct transit if they stay in the port's restricted area. For a Dutch citizen the 30-day unilateral exemption is normally easier: the embassy notices state no third-country onward-ticket condition and no designated-port or area restriction for it. The 240-hour scheme matters mainly if the unilateral policy lapses. The 240-hour scheme started on 17 December 2024, replacing the 72- and 144-hour schemes; it then covered 54 countries and 60 ports in 24 provincial-level regions, and allowed travel between those regions (CCTV, reporting the NIA announcement).

facts.question: Is there an online arrival card, and how do foreigners complete it?
facts.answer: Yes. Since 20 November 2025 foreigners can submit their arrival-card information online before travelling, free of charge. Channels: the NIA website (the Chinese Embassy in the Netherlands gives https://s.nia.gov.cn/ArrivalCardFillingPC/), the NIA government service platform, the 'NIA 12367' app, or the NIA WeChat/Alipay mini programs, or by scanning the official QR code. Travellers who have not done it can still do it on arrival by scanning a QR code, at on-site self-service devices, or on a paper arrival card, which remains available. Seven groups are exempt, including holders of a Foreign Permanent Resident ID card, Hong Kong/Macao travel-permit holders, group-visa travellers, 24-hour direct-transit passengers, same-ship cruise passengers, e-channel users and foreign transport crew. NIA warns that scam sites imitate the service and charge fees; use only the official channels.

facts.question: Must a foreign visitor register their accommodation, e.g. when staying in a private home with a partner's family instead of a hotel?
facts.answer: Yes. Under Article 39 of China's Exit and Entry Administration Law, hotels register their foreign guests, so a hotel guest has nothing extra to do. When a foreigner stays anywhere other than a hotel, such as the home of a partner's family, the foreigner or the host must register the stay with the local public security organ within 24 hours of arrival. Registration is done at the local police station, or at a police office or foreigner service station where one exists. Foreigners who entered visa-free must also register. Failing to register can lead to a warning and a fine of up to CNY 2,000 (Article 76).

facts.question: Can the accommodation registration for a private-home stay be done online (2026)?
facts.answer: Yes. It has been available nationwide since 21 September 2026 (NIA), after a pilot from 20 March 2026 in Hebei, Liaoning, Zhejiang, Hubei, Guangxi, Chongqing and Sichuan; before that, some places such as Beijing, Shanghai, Hainan and Chongqing ran their own online systems. Channels: the NIA government service platform website, the 'NIA 12367' app, the 'NIA 12367' WeChat mini program, or the Alipay mini program. Online registration has the same legal effect as registering at the police station, and in-person registration at the local police remains available. The host, who knows the residence details, normally files the first registration. A foreigner may file alone only when re-registering at a residence already registered on the platform, or when living in their own property. If online registration fails, go to the local police station in person. A registration record can be looked up afterwards, and the NIA 12367 hotline answers questions.

facts.question: Can foreigners link foreign Visa/Mastercard cards to Alipay and WeChat Pay, and since when?
facts.answer: Yes. Both apps let overseas users link international cards without a mainland Chinese bank account. The broad opening dates from July 2023: WeChat Pay (Weixin Pay) announced it on 20 July 2023 and Alipay on 21 July 2023. On 22 July 2023 Beijing's government listed Visa, Diners Club, Mastercard and JCB for WeChat, and Visa, Diners Club, Mastercard and Discover for Alipay. A more limited opening was reported by Reuters on 6 November 2019. Current lists: Ant Group (March 2025) names Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, Discover, Diners Club International and UnionPay International for Alipay. Shanghai's government (2026) lists Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, Discover and Diners Club International for Weixin Pay. Alipay no longer requires a prepaid account or a Chinese phone number.

facts.question: Is cash (RMB) still accepted, and may merchants refuse it (People's Bank of China rules)?
facts.answer: Yes, cash is legal tender and must be accepted. The 'Regulations on RMB Cash Receipt and Payment Services' (人民币现金收付及服务规定) were issued in December 2025 as PBOC / NDRC / NFRA Announcement [2025] No. 29 and have been in force since 1 February 2026. Fee-collecting bodies and businesses may not refuse cash (except where the law requires non-cash payment), may not ask or induce others to refuse it, and may not discriminate against cash payment. Businesses with staffed checkouts or face-to-face service must accept cash and keep reasonable change. Anyone refused can keep evidence and complain to the local PBOC branch or through city hotlines, and penalised violators are publicly named. Refusing cash was already prohibited before: Article 16 of the Law on the People's Bank of China and Article 3 of the RMB Administration Regulations make the renminbi legal tender that no unit or individual may refuse for any public or private debt in China, and the PBOC has run campaigns against cash refusal since 2018. Practical note: mobile QR payment is the norm, so carry some small RMB notes as a backup rather than as the main way to pay.

facts.question: Can foreign cards be used directly at hotels or big merchants, and at ATMs?
facts.answer: Partly. A PBOC / MOFCOM / SAFE notice of May 2024 requires key venues and merchants (e.g. shopping districts, chain supermarkets, restaurants, duty-free shops) to be able to take mobile payment, domestic and overseas bank cards, and cash. SAFE says foreign cards work on POS terminals at airports, hotels and large commercial areas, but also that foreign cards are still not widely accepted. For cash, bank-branch ATMs accept Visa and Mastercard for RMB withdrawals where the network logo is shown. Withdrawals with overseas cards are generally limited to RMB 3,000 per transaction (Shanghai government, Sept 2026), and the card issuer may set its own limits and fees.

facts.question: Are train tickets electronic, and how does a passport holder get a receipt/invoice?
facts.answer: Yes. China's railways use paperless e-tickets, and you board with the passport used for booking; no paper ticket is needed. An e-invoice can be obtained in the Railway 12306 app or at station windows and self-service machines within 180 days after the trip ends. Passport users can also get e-invoices. Background from CCTV: rail e-invoices started on 1 November 2024; you request one from your own 12306 account within 180 days after the trip ends (or after paying a refund or change fee), so a paper ticket is no longer needed for expense claims. Since 1 October 2025 rail passenger transport uses e-invoices across the board, and a paper itinerary slip (纸质行程信息提示单) is still available.

facts.question: Which internet services are blocked in mainland China?
facts.answer: The Dutch government's travel advice for China (last changed 28 Aug 2026; shown as still valid on 20 Oct 2026, or on 1 Nov 2026 in another snapshot) says some internet services are always blocked, for example Google, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube, X and many Dutch and international news media. It also says the Chinese government can temporarily block phone and internet traffic, cutting access to the internet, news, SMS or international phone lines. A community-maintained block list (GFWList, last modified 31 Oct 2026) independently lists all of these services, and also nos.nl, bbc.com and nytimes.com.

facts.question: What are the emergency numbers in mainland China (110, 120, 119, 122), and how do you call them?
facts.answer: 110 = police, 119 = fire, 120 = ambulance (pre-hospital medical emergency): verified against two independent sources, Android's emergency-number database (CN: 110 POLICE, 120 AMBULANCE, 119 FIRE) and Chinese local regulations (Tianjin 2021: 'this city's pre-hospital emergency call number is 120'; Tianjin 2024: '119 fire alarm'; Zhejiang: the police '110 alarm service'), plus Google's libphonenumber, which marks 110, 119 and 120 as emergency numbers. 122: official local regulations list it among the alarm platforms together with 110 and 119, and libphonenumber marks it as an expanded emergency number; that it reaches the traffic police for road accidents is UNVERIFIED (background knowledge). Dial the short number directly from a mobile phone or landline; libphonenumber marks all four as toll-free. Android lists 112 as China's fallback emergency number; whether 112 dialled from a Dutch phone reaches Chinese emergency services is UNVERIFIED, so use 110, 120 or 119.
